content: 1. Discontinue strong CYP3A inhibitors for 3-5 half-lives before initiating therapy with indinavir. 2. Lasmiditan increases indinavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 3. Indinavir increases lefamulin levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid combining lefamulin with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 4. Indinavir increases lemborexant levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid combining lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 5. Indinavir increases leniolisib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Indinavir may alter estrogen plasma levels when coadministered with levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Use nonhormonal contraceptives instead. 7. Indinavir increases lorlatinib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for 3 plasma half-lives. 8. Lorlatinib decreases indinavir levels or effects by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 9. Discontinue antiretroviral therapy (ART) at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed when using lovotibeglogene autotemcel. Long-acting ARTs may require a longer discontinuation period. ARTs may interfere with lovotibeglogene autotemcel manufacturing. 10. Indinavir increases lurbinectedin levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 11. Indinavir increases macitentan levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid combining macitentan with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 12. Indinavir increases mefloquine levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Increased toxicity risk. Avoid coadministration during and for 15 weeks after discontinuing mefloquine. 13. Indinavir increases methylergonovine levels by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 14. Indinavir increases midazolam levels by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 15. Indinavir increases intranasal midazolam levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic midazolam exposure, prolonging sedation. 16. Indinavir increases midostaurin levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions, especially during the first week of treatment. 17. Indinavir increases nefazodone levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Nelfinavir increases indinavir levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 19. Indinavir increases neratinib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid combining neratinib with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 20. Indinavir increases nirogacestat levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Nizatidine decreases indinavir levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Indinavir increases olaparib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce olaparib dose to 150 mg (capsule) or 100 mg (tablet) twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. 23. Indinavir increases omaveloxolone levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day and monitor closely for adverse effects. 24. Omeprazole decreases indinavir levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 25. Indinavir increases osimertinib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If no alternative exists, monitor closely for adverse effects. 26. Indinavir increases oxycodone levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Dose reduction of oxycodone may be warranted. 27. Indinavir increases palbociclib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. 28. Indinavir increases palovarotene levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 29. Pantoprazole decreases indinavir levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 30. Indinavir increases pazopanib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. 31. Indinavir increases pemigatinib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce pemigatinib dose as per drug monograph. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for 3 elimination half-lives. 32. Indinavir increases pexidartinib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce pexidartinib dose as per drug monograph. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for 3 elimination half-lives. 33. Indinavir increases pimavanserin levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce pimavanserin dose to 17 mg/day. 34. Indinavir increases pimozide levels by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of QT interval prolongation. 35. Indinavir increases pirtobrutinib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib during strong CYP3A inhibitor use. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 5 half-lives. 36. Indinavir increases pomalidomide levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 37. Indinavir increases ponatinib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the starting dose of ponatinib to 30 mg daily. 38. Indinavir increases pralsetinib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 39. Indinavir increases quazepam levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 40. Quinidine increases indinavir levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 41. Rabeprazole decreases indinavir levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 42. Indinavir increases ranolazine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 43. Indinavir increases red yeast rice levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. This combination may increase creatine kinase levels and the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis due to the presence of monacolin K (identical to lovastatin) in red yeast rice. 44. Indinavir increases repotrectinib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Discontinue strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors and wait 3-5 elimination half-lives before initiating repotrectinib. 45. Indinavir increases ribociclib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the ribociclib starting dose to 400 mg/day. 46. Rifabutin decreases indinavir levels or effects by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Indinavir increases rifabutin levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 47. Rifampin decreases indinavir levels by increasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 48. Rifapentine decreases indinavir levels by increasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 49. Indinavir increases rimegepant levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 50. Indinavir increases riociguat levels or effects. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor for signs of hypotension and reduce the dose if needed. 51. Indinavir increases rivaroxaban levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid combining rivaroxaban with P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors due to increased bleeding risk. 52. Indinavir increases romidepsin levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid combining romidepsin with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors if possible. 53. Indinavir increases rosuvastatin toxicity by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase the risk of myopathy. 54. Indinavir increases ruxolitinib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Reduce the starting dose to 10 mg twice daily if platelet count is ≥100 x 10^9/L and a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is used. Avoid use if platelet count is <100 x 10^9/L. 55. Indinavir increases selpercatinib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 56. Indinavir increases selumetinib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce selumetinib dosage as per the drug monograph. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for 3 elimination half-lives. 57. Indinavir increases silodosin levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 58. Indinavir increases siponimod levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid combining siponimod with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitors. 59. Indinavir increases sirolimus levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 60. Sodium bicarbonate decreases indinavir levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 61. Sodium citrate/citric acid decreases indinavir levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 62. Indinavir increases sonidegib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid combining sonidegib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 63. Sotorasib decreases indinavir levels or effects by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, refer to the prescribing information for dosage modifications. 64. Indinavir and sparsentan may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment. When resuming sparsentan, consider dose titration. 65. St. John’s Wort decreases indinavir levels by increasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 66. Indinavir increases suvorexant levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
